title: How Does a Tick Hold On So Tight? 🪝
description:
How does a tick hold on so tight? A tick snips your skin with scissor-like chelicerae, anchors a barbed spear called the hypostome, and many ticks glue it in with cement made from their saliva, within minutes of biting.

Sources:
https://web.uri.edu/tickencounter/uncategorized/when-i-pulled-this-tick-off-my-skin-came-with-it/
https://daily.jstor.org/the-science-of-ticks
https://www.livescience.com/4419-sex-fattens-female-ticks-100-times-normal-size.html

topic: How does a tick hold on so tight?
script:
A tick glues itself into your skin in thirty minutes,
and you never feel it.
First, two tiny scissor blades
snip a hole in your skin.
Then it slides in a spear called the hypostome,
covered in barbs that point backwards,
like a fishhook.
Once it's in, it won't slide back out.
Now the wild part.
Within minutes,
some ticks start oozing saliva
that hardens into cement,
a little cone of glue around the spear.
And that spit carries a painkiller,
so you don't notice a thing.
It can hang on for a week or more,
and some females swell up
to a hundred times their size.
When it's full,
it breaks free from its own glue in a minute or two,
and drops off.
So which grip is scarier,
the barbs or the glue?
key_facts: Hard ticks cut into skin with scissor-like chelicerae and insert a hypostome with backward-pointing barbs (URI TickEncounter; JSTOR Daily)
Some ticks begin secreting cement from their salivary glands within 5-30 minutes; it hardens around the mouthparts (URI TickEncounter)
Tick saliva contains anesthetic chemicals so the bite is usually painless (JSTOR Daily)
Ixodes ticks typically feed for about 4-10 days (Narasimhan et al. 2020)
After mating, a female of one ixodid species swells to about 100 times her size (LiveScience, Kaufman)
When full, ticks can separate their mouthparts from the cement in as little as 1-2 minutes (URI TickEncounter)
